(Oshkosh, Wisconsin) | college = [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] (2018–2020) | highlights = * Second-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2020) | medaltemplates= {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 Greece]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Tyrese Haliburton''' (born February 29, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|2}} and {{convert|175|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[point guard]] position. Born in [[Oshkosh, Wisconsin]], Haliburton was a consensus three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] from [[Oshkosh North High School]], whom he led to a state championship in his senior season. As a freshman with [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], he set the program's single-game [[assist (basketball)|assists]] record. He had breakout success as a sophomore and was named to the second team All-[[Big 12 Conference]] despite suffering a season-ending wrist injury. In 2019, Haliburton led the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] to a gold medal and earned all-tournament team honors at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece. ==High school career== Haliburton played basketball for [[Oshkosh North High School]] in [[Oshkosh, Wisconsin]]. As a sophomore, he was named to the All-[[Fox Valley Association]] (FVA) second team and defensive team.{{cite web |title=McCabe top player in FVA |url=https://www.postcrescent.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2016/03/23/mccabe-leads-fva-basketball-team/82192134/ |website=[[The Post-Crescent]] |accessdate=April 29, 2020 |date=March 23, 2016}} In his junior season, Haliburton averaged 18 [[point (basketball)|points]], six [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and five [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, earning FVA Player of the Year and Wisconsin Basketball Coaches Association (WBCA) Division I All-State accolades.{{cite web |title=Tyrese Haliburton |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/h/haliburton-tyrese.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=June 20, 2019}}{{cite web |title=WBCA announces Division 1 Boys Basketball All-State Team |url=https://www.wissports.net/news_article/show/771952 |publisher=Wisconsin Sports Network |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=March 20, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Steve |title=Oshkosh North boys basketball coach Frank Schade retires |url=https://www.thenorthwestern.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2017/04/27/schade-steps-down-oshkosh-north/100974318/ |website=[[Oshkosh Northwestern]] |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=April 27, 2017}} As a senior, he averaged 22.9 points, 6.2 assists, 5.1 rebounds, 3.5 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] and 1.7 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] per game, leading Oshkosh North to a 26–1 record.{{cite web |title=Tyrese Haliburton |url=https://cyclones.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=10430 |publisher=Iowa State Cyclones |accessdate=June 30, 2019}} On February 18, 2018, he scored a career-high 42 points in a win over [[Kaukauna High School]].{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Steve |title=Haliburton fuels No. 1 Oshkosh North's win over No. 1 Kaukauna in FVA showdown |url=https://www.thenorthwestern.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2018/02/16/haliburton-fuels-no-1-oshkosh-norths-win-over-no-1-kaukauna-fva-showdown/345364002/ |website=[[Oshkosh Northwestern]] |accessdate=April 30, 2020 |date=February 16, 2018}} Haliburton scored 31 points, including 24 in the second half, and shot 18–of–18 from the [[free throw]] line in a [[Wisconsin Interscholastic Athletic Association]] Division I state championship victory over [[Brookfield East High School]], his program's first state title.{{cite web |last1=Kabelowsky |first1=Art |title=Tyrese Haliburton's second-half free throws lead Oshkosh North past Brookfield East in the WIAA Division 1 boys basketball final |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/tyrese-haliburton-s-second-half-free-throws-lead-oshkosh-north/article_0793408f-dc12-5a19-b6f9-3122b964cad9.html |website=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |accessdate=April 30, 2020 |date=March 18, 2018}} He was named ''[[Oshkosh Northwestern]]'' All-Area Player of the Year,{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Steve |title=Oshkosh all-area boys basketball: Tyrese Haliburton completes dream season with state title |url=https://www.thenorthwestern.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/31/oshkosh-all-area-boys-basketball-tyrese-haliburton-completes-dream-season-state-title/471792002/ |website=[[Oshkosh Northwestern]] |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=March 31, 2018}} Wisconsin [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]],{{cite web |last1=Rodig |first1=Ryan |title=Haliburton named Gatorade State Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.wearegreenbay.com/sports/highschoolsports/haliburton-named-gatorade-state-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |publisher=[[WFRV-TV]] |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=March 8, 2018}} and FVA co-Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Radcliffe |first1=JR |title=How will history remember the 2018 Mr. Basketball Decision? |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/communities/southwest/sports/2018/03/19/radcliffe-how-history-remember-2018-mr-basketball-decision/436438002/ |website=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=March 19, 2018}} Haliburton was selected to the WBCA Division I All-State team and the ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA Wisconsin first team.{{cite web |title=WBCA announces Division 1 Boys Basketball All-State Team |url=https://www.wissports.net/news_article/show/898903 |publisher=Wisconsin Sports Network |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=March 19, 2018}} ===Recruiting=== 2017.{{cite web |title=Tyrese Haliburton, North, Point Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Tyrese-Haliburton-84658/high-school-146569/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=June 30, bball = yes }} ==College career== On November 6, 2018, Haliburton made his college debut for Iowa State, posting 12 points, four rebounds, and four assists in a 79–53 win over [[Alabama State Hornets men's basketball|Alabama State]].{{cite web |title=Cyclones Open Season With Win Over Alabama State |url=https://cyclones.com/news/2018/11/6/mens-basketball-cyclones-open-season-with-win-over-alabama-state.aspx |publisher=Iowa State Cyclones |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=November 6, 2018}} He scored a season-high 16 points in an 82–55 victory against [[Omaha Mavericks men's basketball|Omaha]] on November 26.{{cite web |title=Cyclones Down Omaha, 82–55 |url=https://cyclones.com/news/2018/11/26/mens-basketball-cyclones-down-omaha-82-55.aspx |publisher=Iowa State Cyclones |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=November 26, 2018}} On December 9, Haliburton recorded 15 points and 17 assists, with one turnover, in a 101–65 win over [[Southern Jaguars men's basketball|Southern]].{{cite web |title=Haliburton Breaks Assist Mark In 101–65 Win Over Southern |url=https://cyclones.com/news/2018/12/9/mens-basketball-haliburton-breaks-assist-mark-in-101-65-win-over-southern.aspx |publisher=Iowa State Cyclones |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=December 9, 2018}} His 17 assists were the most by an Iowa State player in any game, surpassing the previous record set by Eric Heft in 1974.{{cite web |last1=Meredith |first1=Luke |title=Haliburton’s 17 assists lead Iowa State past Southern 101–65 |url=https://apnews.com/637a858d6a9240a48e2120fb9dfdba8b |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=December 9, 2018}} Through 35 appearances in his freshman season, Haliburton averaged 6.8 points, 3.6 assists, and 1.5 steals per game.{{cite web |title=Tyrese Haliburton Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tyrese-Haliburton/Summary/132168 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=June 30, 2019}} He was the only [[NCAA Division I]] true freshman, other than [[Zion Williamson]], to accumulate at least 50 steals and 30 blocks. Haliburton had an assist-to-turnover ratio of 4.5, which led the [[Big 12 Conference]] and ranked second in Division I. Haliburton was named Big 12 Player of the Week on November 11, 2019, during his sophomore season, after averaging 13.5 points and 13.0 assists in wins over [[Mississippi Valley State Delta Devils men's basketball|Mississippi Valley State]] and [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]].{{cite news |title=Haliburton and Holyfield Earn Season’s First Weekly Awards |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2019/11/11/mens-basketball-halliburton-and-holyfield-earn-seasons-first-weekly-awards.aspx |accessdate=November 12, 2019 |work=Big 12 Conference |date=November 11, 2019}} On November 27, he scored a season-high 25 points, to go with nine rebounds and five assists, in an 83–76 loss to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] at the [[Battle 4 Atlantis]].{{cite web |last1=Peterson |first1=Randy |title=Haliburton stars during Iowa State's Battle 4 Atlantis loss against Michigan |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/randy-peterson/2019/11/27/tyrese-haliburton-best-player-iowa-state-battle-4-atlantis-loss-michigan/4317889002/ |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |accessdate=April 30, 2020 |date=November 27, 2019}} On January 4, 2020, Haliburton recorded 22 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists in an [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]] loss to [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]], the first [[double (basketball)|triple-double]] by an Iowa State player since [[Monté Morris]] in 2016.{{cite web |last1=Hines |first1=Travis |title=Cyclones lose Big 12 opener despite Tyrese Haliburton's triple-double |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/2020/01/04/iowa-state-basketball-tyrese-haliburtons-triple-double-not-enough-loss-tcu/2816234001/ |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |accessdate=January 6, 2020 |date=January 4, 2020}} He was subsequently named Big 12 Player of the Week for the second time.{{cite web |title=Iowa State men’s basketball: Tyrese Haliburton named Big 12 player of the week |url=https://www.amestrib.com/sports/20200106/iowa-state-mens-basketball-tyrese-haliburton-named-big-12-player-of-week |website=[[Ames Tribune]] |accessdate=April 30, 2020 |date=January 6, 2020}} After fracturing his left wrist on February 8 during a game against [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], Haliburton was ruled out for the rest of the season. He averaged 15.2 points, 5.9 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 2.5 steals per game as a sophomore.{{cite news |title=Iowa State star Tyrese Haliburton out for season with wrist injury |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28671960/iowa-state-star-tyrese-haliburton-season-wrist-injury |accessdate=February 10, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 10, 2020}} Haliburton was named to the second team All-Big 12.{{cite web |title=Men’s Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced |url=https://big12sports.com/documents/2020/3/8//All_Big_12_Release_19_20_.pdf |website=[[Big 12 Conference]] |accessdate=March 8, 2020 |date=March 8, 2020}} After the season, he announced that he would enter the [[2020 NBA draft]] and forgo his remaining college basketball eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Goldberg |first1=Rob |title=Iowa State's Tyrese Haliburton Declares for 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2876242-iowa-states-tyrese-haliburton-declares-for-2020-nba-draft |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=April 30, 2020 |date=March 24, 2020}} ==National team career== Haliburton played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece.{{cite web |last1=Peterson |first1=Randy |title=Iowa State's Tyrese Haliburton makes USA's World Cup basketball team |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/randy-peterson/2019/06/20/team-usa-u-19-world-cup-tyrese-haliburton/1511411001/ |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=June 20, 2019}} On June 30, he scored a team-high 21 points, shooting 8–of–9 from the field, in a 102–84 group stage win over [[Lithuania men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Lithuania]].{{cite web |title=Haliburton Leads USA Past Lithuania |url=https://cyclones.com/news/2019/6/30/mens-basketball-haliburton-leads-usa-past-lithuania.aspx |publisher=Iowa State Cyclones |accessdate=June 30, 2019 |date=June 30, 2019}} Haliburton averaged 7.9 points and 6.9 assists per game, shooting 69 percent from the field. He led the United States to a gold medal and was named to the all-tournament team.{{cite web |title=Haliburton A Gold Medalist; Earns Spot On All-Star Five |url=https://cyclones.com/news/2019/7/7/mens-basketball-haliburton-a-gold-medalist-earns-spot-on-all-star-five.aspx |publisher=Iowa State Cyclones |accessdate=July 7, 2019 |date=July 7, 2019}}
